The configuration is also highly heterogeneous and anisotropic—a few hub points with $\sim29$ contacts beside points with $\sim9$, visible as a dense core with outliers in the PCA contact graph. It is missing the balanced, symmetric, positive-stress contact structure expected of a substantially better optimum: no free/flexible points, no orbit or antipodal symmetry, and no collective mode that redistributes load away from the hubs.

diagnosis: The only gain over the record is $1.95\times10^{-7}$, essentially LP-polishing noise after 65 programs. The plots explain why: over a thousand pairs sit at slack $\sim10^{-16}$, every point has 9–29 contacts and there are zero rattlers, so this is a massively over-constrained, rigid jammed glass with more active constraints than the $176\cdot8-36$ effective degrees of freedom. Random per-point kicks or deleting a few points either snap back to the same contact topology or destroy too much structure, while recent programs repeatedly paid for LP polishes inside the search loop and timed out at 200s before sampling more than a handful of basins. Structurally, the configuration is amorphous and stress-heterogeneous (some points carry 28 contacts, others 9, with a lopsided PCA projection): it lacks the balanced, near-uniform contact/stress pattern — plausibly with few distinct inner-product levels or approximate symmetry — expected of a genuinely better optimum.
